Upstream GCC commit 5d419c69ce2e6b86d7da75f18736904885674219 (PR libstdc++/124370) stops std::bitset wide-character stream extraction from sizing its buffer without sizeof(wchar_t). The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, re-expressed against the 14.2.0 operator>>. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-115455

Upstream GCC commit 2fd8866591b5aea7098835f80ab7e176382175ae makes std::vector<bool> constructors check the element count against max_size() before sizing the bit array, so the word count cannot wrap. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, without the from_range constructor hunk, which GCC 14.2.0 does not have. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114691

Upstream GCC commit c1f32b67510f6f9998deadaef5090b6663adb979 sizes the parallel std::search border table one element larger so the border computation cannot index past it. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114690

Debian security tracker: fixed in unstable by the same change as CVE-2026-85091, which is upstream zlib commit df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148. That change resets the stream input pointer and available input after a failed write() in gz_write(), so a later gz* write cannot use the stale caller buffer. This package build includes an adaptation of that upstream change for the zlib 1.3.1 code base. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-76844

CVE-2026-93753 affects npm deepmerge through 4.3.1, which remains the latest release on the public npm registry, and GitHub GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 lists no patched version. The component appears in the temporalio-ui-server SPDX SBOM generated from the pruned production node_modules tree at image build time. The runtime image ships the Go ui-server binary and static assets under /home/ui-server, not node_modules. Assessment is pending until upstream publishes a fixed deepmerge release or reachability in the shipped artifact is ruled out with evidence.

GitHub Security Advisory and Scout report the fix in @sveltejs/kit 3.0.0. Temporal UI pins @sveltejs/kit to a 2.x release for compatibility with its Svelte 5 and Vite 6 toolchain; overriding to Kit 3.0.0 fails svelte-kit sync because Kit 3 expects Vite APIs (parseSync) not provided by the pinned Vite 6 line. A major Kit upgrade needs upstream Temporal UI alignment and full build and browser test validation before it can ship.

GO-2026-5932 is scoped exclusively to the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package tree (and subpackages), which is frozen upstream with no fixed module release. Scout matches golang.org/x/crypto at the module level because the advisory records the module with no fixed version. Analysis of this image's shipped Go binaries found no import or link of golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp; the vulnerable OpenPGP code is therefore not present in the shipped artifacts (vulnerable_code_not_present).
Marked no-dsa by Debian Security Team; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-89092

The covered package builds prevent a failed direct-buffer gzwrite from leaving a caller-owned input pointer available to gzprintf or gzvprintf. They either guard the later formatting entry points or include the pointer-state reset from upstream commit https://github.com/madler/zlib/commit/df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148 in the equivalent zlib 1.3.1 error branch. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-85091.

GO-2026-5932 is scoped exclusively to the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package tree, which is frozen upstream with no fixed module release; see https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5932. The docker-engine APK ships dockerd built from Moby 29.7.2, which vendors github.com/ProtonMail/go-crypto for OpenPGP and does not import golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp. go version -m on the published dockerd binary lists golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0 as a module dependency but no golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp import path, so the advisory OpenPGP code is not present in the shipped artifact.

The vulnerability is in esbuild's Deno module (lib/deno/mod.ts), which downloads a native binary without SHA-256 integrity verification. The esbuild npm package shipped here contains only the Node.js distribution (install.js, lib/main.js); the Deno module is published separately and is not part of the package, and the image has no Deno runtime. The vulnerable code is therefore not present in what this image ships.

This CVE is only affecting installation on PowerPC architecture and even then is this CVE disputed because the OpenSSL security policy explicitly notes that any side channels which require same physical system to be detected are outside of the threat model for the software. The timing signal is so small that it is infeasible to be detected without having the attacking process running on the same physical system.

Fault injection based attacks are not within OpenSSLs threat model according to the security policy and this CVE is not treated as security bug by upstream: https://www.openssl.org/policies/general/security-policy.html
